children: While New Zealand-based retailer Warehouse's refreshed strategy is sensible, delivery will be more challenging, Forsyth Barr says. That's because of a subdued domestic consumer backdrop, historic underinvestment in stores, and the need to replace legacy systems. "As such, we do not expect the market to rerate Warehouse until it can demonstrate consistent execution and drive positive earnings momentum," analyst Paul Laxton Koraua says. Warehouse is targeting 100 million New Zealand dollars of operating profit within 3-5 years. It signaled that could come from better profit margins in the Red Shed business, like-for-like sales growth and the opening of new stores. Forsyth Barr retains a neutral call and a NZ$0.75/share price target on Warehouse. The stock is little changed at NZ$0.68. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
